title: Saving and Loading Models 💾
description: Master SavedModel, HDF5, and weights‑only formats to persist your trained models.

slides.title: Why Save? 📦
slides.content:
# Training is Expensive – Don't Lose It!

After hours (or days) of training, you need to **persist** the model to:
- Share with colleagues or the community.
- Deploy to production (server, mobile, browser).
- Resume training later.
- Keep a checkpoint for safety.

TensorFlow offers multiple formats, but the **SavedModel** format is the standard for serving.

slides.title: Saving Formats Overview 📋
slides.content:
# Three Main Options

1. **SavedModel** (directory) – contains the complete model (architecture, weights, computation graph). Used for **TensorFlow Serving**, TF Hub, TF.js, and TFLite.
2. **HDF5** (`.h5` file) – single file, Keras‑native. Good for checkpointing, but less portable.
3. **Weights‑only** – only the values (no architecture). Use `model.save_weights('weights/')`.

> Analogy: SavedModel is a fully assembled, ready‑to‑cook meal kit; HDF5 is a frozen meal that works in your microwave (Keras).

slides.title: Saving a Keras Model
slides.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf

model = tf.keras.Sequential([
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='relu', input_shape=(784,)),
    tf.keras.layers.Dense(10, activation='softmax')
])
model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='sparse_categorical_crossentropy')
# train...
model.save('my_model')  # creates folder with assets, variables, saved_model.pb

quizData.question: Which saving format is preferred for TensorFlow Serving?
quizData.explanation: SavedModel is the standard format for deployment, containing the complete graph and signature definitions.

slides.title: Loading a SavedModel
slides.codeSnippet:
loaded = tf.keras.models.load_model('my_model')
# Ready for inference or continued training
print(loaded.predict(test_data))

slides.title: Saving & Loading Weights Only ⚖️
slides.content:
# When You Need Flexibility

`model.save_weights('checkpoint/')` writes checkpoints (can be used with `tf.train.Checkpoint`).

Restore with `model.load_weights('checkpoint/')`. Useful for:
- Transfer learning (load pre‑trained weights into a different architecture).
- Continuing training after a crash.

> Note: The architecture must be re‑created in code before loading weights.

slides.title: Custom Objects 🧩
slides.content: If your model uses custom layers or losses, you must pass them to `load_model` via `custom_objects` dict, or save in the newer Keras v3 format that includes everything.
